cards.text: Welcome to the bakery, friend, where today's batch is Proverbs 19, part of the proverbs of Solomon, king of Israel (Prov 1:1; 10:1). These are short sayings, one right after another. First up, Solomon sets two people side by side: a poor man who walks with integrity, and a fool whose lips are perverse.

cards.question: A poor man with integrity or a fool with perverse lips. Which one does Solomon say is better?

cards.text: Next, Solomon warns that he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark. Friend, I once got so fired up I slid a WHOLE batch into the oven before turning it on, then stood there forty minutes waiting on raw dough.

cards.question: Rushing ahead misses the mark. Solomon says even zeal is no good without ___

cards.text: Then Solomon says a man's own folly subverts his way. That's me tripping over my OWN gold base, then spinning around to see who pushed me.

cards.question: His own folly wrecked his way, yet his heart rages against the ___

cards.text: Now Solomon gets real about money and friendship. And he doesn't sugarcoat it, friend, and I say that as a guy who sugarcoats for a LIVING.

cards.question: Solomon says wealth attracts many friends.

cards.text: But a poor man is deserted by his friend. Then Solomon turns to the courtroom, where a false witness takes the stand.

cards.question: Solomon says a false witness will get away with it.

cards.text: Back to friends. Many seek the favor of the prince, and I bet that prince's phone NEVER stops buzzing.

cards.question: Solomon says everyone is a friend of whom?

cards.text: Walk in carrying a box of cookies and the WHOLE room suddenly remembers your birthday. But the poor man? All his brothers hate him, so how much more do his friends avoid him.

cards.question: When the poor man goes after his friends, pleading, they come running back.

cards.text: Now Solomon makes a pitch for wisdom. And friend, the pitch is so good even a selfish guy would sign up.

cards.question: Solomon says the one who acquires wisdom is doing what?
Solomon says one who safeguards understanding will find ___

cards.text: Then Solomon brings the false witness right back: he will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish. When a line comes back like that, friend, write it on your apron.
Stop two, friend! Solomon kicks off with things that just don't fit, starting with this: luxury is unseemly for a fool.

cards.question: Solomon says one thing is even worse than a fool living in luxury. What is it?

cards.text: Next, Solomon says a man's insight gives him patience. Good, because I have stared down an oven timer and yelled at it to HURRY UP.

cards.question: A man's insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to ___ an offense

cards.text: Overlooking an offense? Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm still not mad at anybody. Meanwhile, Solomon says a king's rage is like the roar of a lion.

cards.question: Solomon says a king's favor is just as scary as his rage.

cards.text: Nope, his favor is like dew on the grass, so if the lion's roaring, friend, wait for the DEW. Then Solomon walks into the home, where a foolish son is his father's ruin.

cards.question: What does Solomon compare a quarrelsome wife to?

cards.text: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers. Me? All I ever got was a price sticker that said 25 cents.

cards.question: Houses and wealth come from fathers. Where does Solomon say a prudent wife comes from?

cards.text: Now, laziness. Solomon says laziness brings on deep sleep, and friend, me and the snooze button have a LONG history.

cards.question: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer ___

cards.text: Then Solomon sets two paths side by side: he who keeps a commandment preserves his soul. I follow a recipe card like it's a treasure map, friend, EVERY step.

cards.question: Solomon says he who is careless in his ways will die.

cards.text: And here's one that makes this old stamper grin from mustache to mustache. It's about being kind to the poor.

cards.question: What does Solomon call kindness to the poor?
Solomon says the LORD will repay the one who is kind to the poor.

cards.text: Then a word on raising a son: discipline him, for in that there is hope, and do not be party to his death. And a man of great anger must pay the penalty.

cards.question: If you rescue a man of great anger, you will have to do so ___

cards.text: Last stop, friend! Solomon says to listen to counsel and accept discipline, which is tough for a guy who once argued with a recipe card and LOST.

cards.question: Why does Solomon say to listen to counsel and accept discipline?

answers.text: So you'll be wise the rest of your days
So you'll be rich the rest of your days
So people will praise you all your days

cards.text: Then comes the big one: many plans are in a man's heart. I keep a sticky note on every oven, friend, EVERY oven, so I know a thing or two about plans.

cards.question: Solomon says a man's own plans are what will prevail in the end.

cards.text: Nope, the purpose of the LORD will prevail. Friend, I had ONE plan: sit on the Millers' counter forever, and look at me now, a stamper with his own PLANET.

cards.question: Solomon says the desire of a man is loving devotion, and it's better to be poor than a ___

cards.text: Then Solomon says the fear of the LORD leads to life. LIFE, friend, and that's coming from a guy who spent years in a drawer thinking his story was over.

cards.question: Solomon says the fear of the LORD lets a person rest content, without visitation from harm.

cards.text: Now my favorite picture in the whole chapter. The slacker buries his hand in the dish.

cards.question: The slacker's hand is in the dish. What does he do next?

answers.text: He won't even bring it back to his mouth
He eats every last bit in one go
He passes the dish to his friends

cards.text: That's reaching into the cookie jar and deciding the trip back up is just TOO much work. Next, Solomon says to strike a mocker, and the simple will beware.

cards.question: What does Solomon say happens when you rebuke a discerning man?

cards.text: Then a hard line: a son who assaults his father or evicts his mother brings shame and disgrace. And the speaker talks straight to "my son" about what happens if he stops hearing instruction.

cards.question: If you cease to hear instruction, you will ___ from the words of knowledge

cards.text: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity the way I go through a bowl of cookie dough. Then Solomon closes with what's waiting for mockers.

cards.question: What does Solomon say is prepared for mockers?
Solomon says beatings are prepared for the backs of fools.

findings.problem: The two right-type answers are people (the poor man, the fool), but the third answer, 'They're both about the same,' is a different kind of thing. It is filler, not a third person, so the question is really a two-option pick.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'Walk in carrying a box of cookies…' / 'But the poor man?' / 'All his brothers hate him…'. It is not the opening card, so it should be one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'Overlooking an offense?' / 'Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer…' / 'Meanwhile, Solomon says a king's rage…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers.' / 'Me?' / 'All I ever got was a price sticker that said 25 cents.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank is just the last word of verse 15 ('hunger'), and the wrong answers 'shame' and 'loss' are equally believable results of idleness. Nothing in card 11 (laziness, deep sleep, the snooze button) points toward hunger. The baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
